title: [ar] Craft over convenience
excerpt: [ar] Rejecting generic SaaS templates in favor of typographic restraint, tactile hover states, and bi-directional prose.
author: Marcus Lind

body.text: [ar] Every tool offers a default path. Modern component libraries often funnel design teams toward the same beige aesthetic: rounded buttons, soft purple shadows, and card carousels. Breaking free of this gravitational pull requires intentional resistance.

[ar] We chose a single high-chroma accent color and paired it with two disparate typographic families: a tight variable grotesque for headlines and an open literary serif for narrative prose. Every interactive element earns its place through utility rather than ornamentation.
[ar] Simplicity is about subtracting the obvious and adding the meaningful.
body.cite: [ar] John Maeda, The Laws of Simplicity

body.text: [ar] Consider the reading experience across different languages and cultures. When a publication respects right-to-left readers natively, the drawer navigates from the left, breadcrumb arrows invert, and typographic measure adjusts naturally.

items: [ar] Audit every element for unnecessary visual noise
[ar] Enforce strict character limits per line to protect reading comfort
[ar] Deliver full semantic markup directly to every visitor

body.text: [ar] True craft is felt in what is left out.
